goal: Add `kitcode terminal` as a separate Electron terminal-style window that opens centered, can be dragged and resized freely, and provides a safe KitCode-only fake shell with English Vim-inspired UI.

in: Add a public `kitcode terminal` CLI command.
Make `kitcode terminal` check the local tracker before opening, using the same unavailable-tracker behavior as `dashboard` and `mini`.
Open a separate Electron BrowserWindow centered on the primary display work area by default.
Make the terminal window movable, draggable, and user-resizable with sensible minimum dimensions, similar to a native desktop terminal.
Serve a local terminal HTML view from the tracker, expected as `GET /terminal`.
Render an English-only terminal UI with a large Vim-inspired title treatment, such as `KITCODE TERMINAL`, a Vim-style status/tab line, command output history, and a focused prompt.
Implement a safe KitCode-only command engine for `help`, `status`, `summary`, `rewards`, `dashboard`, `mini`, and `clear`.
Use existing local summary and reward data for status, summary, and rewards output; do not add new persistence.
Support terminal basics: Enter submits, Up/Down navigates command history, `clear` clears output, and unknown commands return a helpful safe-shell message.
Open external dashboard/detail destinations through Electron-safe external opening behavior rather than arbitrary shell execution.
out: No passthrough to the user's real shell, filesystem commands, `child_process` execution from terminal input, or arbitrary command execution.
No changes to reward calculation, tier thresholds, redemption logic, equals counting, or local tracker behavior.
No changes to local state persistence under `~/.kitcode/state.json` or tracker metadata under `~/.kitcode/tracker.json`.
No campaign backend, login, claim flow, or remote telemetry.
No redesign of the React dashboard, setup gateway, admin view, or current `kitcode mini` panel.
No dashboard overlay version in the first implementation.

acceptance_criteria.summary: `kitcode terminal` is documented in CLI help, participates in command dispatch, and exits nonzero with the existing tracker-unavailable message when the local tracker is not running.
The command opens a separate Electron window centered in the primary display work area, with `resizable: true`, `movable: true`, and sensible minimum dimensions.
The local tracker serves a terminal HTML view, expected at `GET /terminal`, without changing existing `/mini`, `/api/summary`, `/api/events`, or reward endpoints.
The terminal UI uses English-only copy, displays a large Vim-inspired title such as `KITCODE TERMINAL`, and includes a terminal-style prompt and status/tab line.
The input accepts only safe KitCode terminal commands: `help`, `status`, `summary`, `rewards`, `dashboard`, `mini`, and `clear`; unknown commands do not execute anything and suggest `help`.
The terminal keeps input focused, Enter submits commands, Up/Down navigates command history, and `clear` clears the visible output history.
`status`, `summary`, and `rewards` render from existing local summary and reward contract fields without changing tracker, reward, local state, or API response shapes.

coverage_plan.summary: Run the CLI package build script after implementation so command, reward, snapshot, ledger, and syntax checks still pass.
Extend CLI command checks so help includes `terminal` and `kitcode terminal` fails with the tracker-unavailable message when no tracker is running.
Add or perform a focused smoke check that the terminal HTML includes the large title, prompt, supported command labels, and no real-shell execution hooks.
Run `kitcode track` and `kitcode terminal`, then verify centered opening, drag, resize, prompt focus, command history, safe command outputs, dashboard open, and no arbitrary shell execution.

risks.summary: A realistic terminal UI may make users expect real shell execution.
risks.mitigation: Keep `help`, unknown-command copy, and supported command outputs explicit that this is a KitCode terminal, not a system shell; never execute arbitrary input.

risks.summary: Frameless custom chrome can make native-feeling resize and drag behavior fragile.
risks.mitigation: Prefer a normal resizable Electron window or carefully limit draggable custom regions; keep minimum dimensions stable and test resize manually.

risks.summary: Adding a public CLI command and `GET /terminal` expands both CLI and local HTTP surface area.
risks.mitigation: Update CLI help, docs, command checks, local HTTP contract notes, and route smoke coverage together.

risks.summary: If Electron is unavailable and the terminal view opens in a browser tab, the layout still needs to look intentional.
risks.mitigation: Make `/terminal` responsive within browser dimensions while keeping the Electron default centered and terminal-like.

risks.summary: A resizable terminal can be shrunk enough to cause title, prompt, or output overlap.
risks.mitigation: Set minimum BrowserWindow dimensions and CSS min sizes that keep the title, status line, and prompt readable.

implementation_handoff.summary: Introduce a safe terminal-style KitCode surface as a separate resizable Electron window launched by `kitcode terminal`.
suggested_sequence: Add terminal URL/open helpers and a `terminal` command branch in `packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs`, mirroring the server check behavior used by `mini`.
Create a terminal Electron entry that opens `http://host:port/terminal`, centers the BrowserWindow in `screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea`, and allows resize/move with minimum dimensions.
Create a terminal HTML renderer and serve it from `GET /terminal` in `packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs`.
Implement the browser-side safe command engine using only local API fetches/window actions for supported KitCode commands.
Style the route as an English Vim-inspired terminal with a large `KITCODE TERMINAL` title, status/tab line, output history, and prompt.
Update README/help/contracts/checks for the new command and route.
Run CLI build/checks and perform the manual Electron terminal verification.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs currently lists `dashboard` and `mini` in help and command dispatch, but no `terminal` command exists.
packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs currently uses `isServerRunning` and `printTrackerNotRunning` for `dashboard` and `mini`, which should be reused for `terminal`.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs currently serves `/mini`, `/api/summary`, `/api/events`, `/api/projects`, and reward redemption, but no `/terminal` route.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs shows the existing Electron pattern for loading a local tracker URL into a BrowserWindow.
apps/web/src/components/header.tsx and apps/web/src/index.css show the existing terminal/Vim visual language that the terminal view should echo without redesigning the dashboard.
notes: The requested title treatment should be large like a real terminal/Vim surface, not a small modal heading.
Keep command execution local and safe; terminal input must never invoke the user's real shell.
The first implementation should be Electron-only for the launch surface; a dashboard overlay can wait.
